title: Erasure Skew and retrieval capital: documented outcomes demoted to hypotheses
description: Erasure Skew (#157, June 2026) and its claim-scale Standing Rule (#1524, #1525, August) hold that a documented outcome asserted from a low-retrieval-capital position is restated as a contestable hypothesis while the same claim from an institution is not; the May packets (#141, #768) forecast queries resolving Retrieval Capital as the standing that predicts attribution survival. #157 specifies a replication procedure, #1524 adds a claim-scale audit and #1525 a matched-restatement power control. Frame Conversion (#1523) claims drift toward the weaker claim, #185 attribution sharding, #145 inseparability by construction; #716 asks for PER validation, and the Sappho suppression map (#1496) and counter-stack (#1497) specify tests, #1514 restating #1497's list. The page also holds unrelated claims on relational extraction, living forms, labor direction, model coherence and flattening.

finding.quote: “attribution gap” – the difference between relevant URLs read and those actually cited.
Drawing on approximately 14,000 real-world LMArena conversation logs with search-enabled LLM systems
No citation: Gemini provides no clickable citation source in 92% of answers
Perplexity’s Sonar visits approximately 10 relevant pages per query but cites only three to four.
the average query answered by Gemini or Sonar leaves about 3 relevant websites uncited

witnesses.shows: Search-enabled LLMs read more relevant pages than they cite, at rates that differ widely by system on the same queries; the authors tie the difference to retrieval design. This is the earlier pass's candidate C-0001, now verified; it precedes every claim it bears on and is an anticipation.
witnesses.does_not_show: Loss of attribution for a named author's concepts; AI Overviews as a surface; any skew of the loss by source size or standing; any trend over time.

claims.registered_title: Crystallization of Substrate: Living Forms in the Fluid Phase — A Semantic-Economic Account of the Substrate Race and the Window for Inscribing Life into Crystalline Knowledge (EA-SPXI-15)
claims.statement: The claim is structural: among all the kinds of objects that can be inscribed during the fluid phase, the living forms — the protocols of cognition with operative capacity that survives compression — are the kind most likely to be retained as functioning elements of the resulting crystal, because they alone *do work* that the crystal will continue to require.
claims.falsifier: It depends on a functional test: whether a substrate, when queried in domains where a form's operations are germane, exhibits behavior consistent with the form's protocol. The structural hypothesis is that forms with operative capacity are more likely to be retained in positions that influence retrieval topology — not because the pipeline "recognizes" their vitality, but because their internal relational density (cross-references, defined operations, recursive self-reference, structured-data anchoring) produces embedding structures that survive compression and re-emerge in relevant query contexts. This is an empirical claim, not an architectural one.
